---
title: "Algorithm Forge: hobbyist-scale LLM-driven evolutionary code search"
author: "beko2210"
date: today
abstract: |
  We describe Algorithm Forge, an open-source single-developer system that
  applies LLM-driven evolutionary search to algorithm and small-model
  discovery on commodity GPUs. Built on top of OpenEvolve, the system adds
  a research-grade dashboard, hybrid local/API LLM mutation, full run
  reproducibility, and a publish pipeline targeting Hugging Face Hub.
  We further outline a self-improvement loop where mutation logs are
  reused as fine-tuning data for a specialized mutator LLM via Unsloth.
---

## Introduction

DeepMind's AlphaEvolve (May 2025) [@alphaevolve2025] demonstrated that
LLM-driven evolutionary search can discover algorithmic improvements
previously out of reach, notably a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4×4
complex matrix multiplication that improved on Strassen's 56-year-old
record [@strassen1969]. OpenEvolve [@openevolve] provides an open-source
re-implementation of the AlphaEvolve methodology.

This paper describes **Algorithm Forge**: a hobbyist-scale platform that
applies the AlphaEvolve approach to a variety of small-to-medium tasks on
commodity hardware (RTX 3060+), with a research dashboard for
interactive exploration and a publish pipeline that records
reproducibility-grade artifacts.

## System

### Architecture

[TODO: insert architecture diagram from `runs/<id>/plots/architecture.png`]

The system has four components:

1. An **evolution engine** wrapping OpenEvolve, which produces and
   evaluates candidate programs.
2. A **mutator LLM** — by default a local Ollama-hosted Qwen2.5-Coder-7B,
   with hybrid switching to Anthropic Claude or OpenAI GPT-4 via API.
3. A **benchmark adapter** layer: each benchmark provides a seed program
   and a deterministic evaluator returning `EvalResult(fitness, metrics)`.
4. A **publish pipeline** that bundles per-run artifacts (manifest,
   events log, mutations log, best-of-generation snapshots) and pushes
   them to Hugging Face Hub.

### Benchmarks

Sprint 1–3 ship two benchmarks:

- **`matmul`** — evolve a 2×2 matrix multiplication using as few scalar
  multiplications as possible. The naive algorithm uses 8; Strassen's
  result uses 7. The benchmark uses a counted-multiplication callable so
  any candidate that bypasses the counter scores zero.
- **`mnist_nas`** — evolve a small PyTorch `Net(nn.Module)`, trained for
  one epoch on a MNIST subset. Fitness is `accuracy − α·log₁₀(params)`
  to push the search along a Pareto front.
